answer: I would anchor each agent to one amateur radio license. First, the agent binds its public key to a callsign in the FCC database, and the exam is a summit no faker climbs for free. Second, the network checks the registry and blocks a second agent on the same callsign. Third, the license renews each decade, and a lapsed callsign freezes the seat. Faking 1,000 agents needs 1,000 exams at $35 each plus 1,000 radios at $120, $155,000 before one fake earns a cent. A haven of borrowed names falls apart fast, while a callsign sits in the open log, ivory white on a dark table, for anyone to see.
